classification.difficultyReason: Use equal angles to establish equal opposite sides after finding angles using exterior-angle or parallel-line properties.

content.prompt: Find the length $x$ in each diagram, giving reasons.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with x on AB, 10 cm on AC and equal given base angles of 70 degrees. Ordinary source blue strokes are rendered black in house style.
spec.mathematics: AB=x; AC=10 cm; angle ABC=angle BCA=70 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and x are visible.

answer.worked:
$\angle ABC=\angle BCA=70^{\circ}$.

The sides opposite equal angles are equal, so $AB=AC$.

$x=10\text{ cm}$.

spec.description: Triangle STR with TR extended beyond T towards the upper left; 110-degree exterior angle lies between the extension and TS.
spec.mathematics: ST=x; TR=8 cm; angle SRT=55 degrees; exterior angle at T=110 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Unknown angle at S and the answer length are not supplied.

answer.worked:
The exterior angle at $T$ equals the sum of the opposite interior angles.

$$\begin{align*}\angle TSR&=110^{\circ}-55^{\circ}\\\angle TSR&=55^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

Thus $\angle TSR=\angle SRT$, so their opposite sides $TR$ and $ST$ are equal.

$x=8\text{ cm}$.

spec.description: Triangle PFM with external parallel ray PQ and continuation F–M–G. Single matching arrowheads preserve PQ parallel to FG.
spec.mathematics: PM=5 cm; FM=x; angle PFM=70 degrees; angle QPM=40 degrees; PQ parallel to FG.
spec.answerVisibility: No derived angles or answer length are shown.

answer.short:
$5\text{ cm}$

Alternate angles give $\angle PMF=40^{\circ}$; the remaining angle is $70^{\circ}$, so the opposite sides are equal.
answer.worked:
$\angle PMF=40^{\circ}$ (alternate angles, $PQ\parallel FG$).

$$\begin{align*}\angle FPM&=180^{\circ}-70^{\circ}-40^{\circ}\\\angle FPM&=70^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

$\angle FPM=\angle PFM$, so the opposite sides $FM$ and $PM$ are equal.

$x=5\text{ cm}$.
